title: Publish CCP2 requirement-to-evidence traceability
description:
Scope: /home/mark/Developer/lichen-workspace/project-LICHEN/docs/ccp-conformance.md and focused CCP2 rows/page within /home/mark/Developer/lichen-workspace/project-LICHEN/docs/spec-coverage/. Map every CCP2-001 through CCP2-026 requirement to actual production entry points, independent case IDs, exact source/corpus revisions, reproducible commands, raw artifacts and evidence classes from the completed software gates. Use the manifest and result validator as independent inventory checks. Do not resweep unrelated specification chapters or infer integration/RF evidence from helper tests or missing results.

HPC8 execution policy: Code, test, or schema changes require three independent correctness, security, and robustness reviews; file and fix all findings and re-review. Use independent oracles, never weakened legacy tests or self-generated expected results. Preserve upstream Yggdrasil addressing, radio-owned identity, best-effort custody, baseline SCHC, and the human-only OSCORE/EDHOC security edit bar. External actions, hardware/RF operations, and port access require scoped explicit permission and applicable bench safety checks. Research may conclude no-go; an authorization gate requires affirmative, recorded approval for its actual scope. Dependency closure and decomposition are not permission. No speculative activation, including deferred portability or experimental modes.
design: Extend the existing conformance guide and focused coverage layout; add a separate CCP2 page only if needed to preserve historical evidence. Prefer stable symbol/section links over hard-coded line-number claims.
acceptance_criteria: All 26 requirement IDs appear exactly and resolve to applicable case/result artifacts or explicit failed/not-assessed evidence. Production paths and commands exist at the recorded revision; independent corpus and admission-supplement digests match the results. Automated/local structural checks catch missing IDs, stale links and unsupported claim upgrades. Policy-tested, wire-tested, integrated, RF-measured and authorization-reviewed remain separate, and absent hardware/authority evidence is not shown as passed.
